This is a beautiful game from an extremely creative and talented studio.  I love all their previous games and I love combo based skateboarding games and this falls short of being a fully realized version of either.  The controls are floaty and imprecise compared to arcade skating games and compared to the pathless.  The opportunities to do tricks for a reason are so rare and easy to miss, I cannot understand why the trick attack areas are treated like collectibles when they explore the game's mechanics more than the water restoration happening throughout the game.  If this was their first game I would call it promising but it's a huge step back for Giant Squid and it bums me out to say that.  Play abzu or the pathless and if you want an ethereal emotional skateboarding game play skate story.

I really wish people would stop comparing every difficult action/souls-like game to FromSoftware and enjoy what they decided to play.

Hard games and connected levels existed way before Dark Souls/Elden Ring, and fanbases in other genres don't defend their favorite developers this aggressively.

Genres like RTS games are more demanding on your reflexes and brainpower than learning a boss's attack pattern. Also, FromSoft games have their own clunky moments that fans just forgive as being 'intentional.'

I actually enjoy non-FromSoft Souls-likes more, and The First Berserker: Khazan nails it with amazing art and great boss fights. Outside of a cluttered loot system, it’s a fun game to play if you judge it on its own merits.

I like these games, with Until Dawn being the best in the series, but this is lame compared to that. There’s no atmosphere thanks to the corny music between episodes, and the acting, directing and story is bad. It’s a cool concept as I love The Thing but executed poorly. 

I actually liked the stealth mechanics, as it added a new layer of gameplay, but the QTEs have been massively reduced, and I actually felt like I interacted with the game way more less that it’s predecessors.

Reminds me of Judge Dredd 2012, except it's Robocop. This game would have been a 7 out of 10, but I kept having crashes and losing progress because some of the saves are stretched out and you can't make your own saves. Gameplay is overall the same as the first game, which is good shooting and fighting, but the story is again meh, just like the first one. I still really don't like the Unreal MetaHumans they use for all the characters. I found myself not really using any of the other upgrades I got for the pistol besides the first full auto mod, since that one's just the best. Anyway, this game overall is probably a 6 out of 10. It's definitely just an okay game id recommend to pick it up only on a sale unless your a super Robocop fan. Man I'm glad that I'm done with this series.
